'''Rebecca Bennett''' (born March 13, 1987) is an American healthcare executive and former [[United States Navy|Navy]] helicopter pilot who is the [[U.S. representative]]-elect for {{ushr|NJ|7}}. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], Bennett defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Thomas Kean Jr.]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 7|2026 election]].

==Early life and education==
Rebecca Bennett was born on March 13, 1987,<ref name=":1"/><ref>{{Cite tweet|number=2032554996231741669|user=RebeccaForNJ07|title=All I want for my birthday this year is to flip this seat and take back the House. Can you chip in $13 to help me send Tom Kean Jr. packing?|first=Rebecca|last=Bennett|date=March 13, 2026|access-date=September 27, 2026}}</ref> and was raised by a conservative family in [[Granbury, Texas]].<ref name=":2">{{cite web|last=Friedman|first=Matt|date=February 4, 2025|title=Former Navy helicopter pilot looks to take on Kean|url=https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2025/02/former-navy-helicopter-pilot-looks-to-take-on-kean-00202342|url-access=subscription|publisher=[[Politico#Politico_Pro|Politico Pro]]|access-date=June 8, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Texas">{{cite web |title=A Democratic former Navy pilot wins primary to try unseating Tom Kean Jr. in NJ's most contested House race |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/02/a-democratic-former-navy-pilot-wins-primary-to-try-unseating-tom-kean-jr-in-new-jerseys-most-contested-house-race-00947722 |website=POLITICO |access-date=6 June 2026 |language=en |date=2 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="Up1">{{cite web |last1=Snowflack |first1=Fred |title=CD-7 Flashpoint: Bennett, in Gear |url=https://www.insidernj.com/cd-7-flashpoint-bennett-in-gear/ |website=Insider NJ |access-date=6 June 2026 |date=8 May 2026}}</ref> She attended the [[Texas Academy of Mathematics and Science]] before graduating from [[Cornell University]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in 2009.<ref name="Cornell">{{cite web |title=Navy Veteran, Mother, Rebecca Bennett '09 Runs for Congress in New Jersey |url=https://www.cornellsun.com/article/2025/10/navy-veteran-mother-rebecca-bennett-09-runs-for-congress-in-new-jersey |website=The Cornell Sun |access-date=6 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="Ballot">{{cite web |title=Rebecca Bennett (New Jersey) |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Rebecca_Bennett_(New_Jersey) |website=Ballotpedia |access-date=6 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref> She later earned a [[Master of Business Administration]] from the [[University of Pennsylvania]]'s [[Wharton School]].<ref name="Cornell" />
==Career==
===Military===
[[File:Littoral combat ship USS Independence (LCS 2), RIMPAC 2014 (Image 3 of 3).jpg|thumb|upright=1|Bennett preparing an [[MH-60S Seahawk]] helicopter during [[RIMPAC]] in 2014]]
After graduating from Cornell in 2009, Bennett joined the [[United States Navy]], where she became a [[Naval aviator (United States)|naval aviator]].<ref name="Daughter"/> She later trained at the [[United States Naval Test Pilot School]], becoming the 18th female [[test pilot]] in the U.S. Navy.<ref name="Spotlight">{{cite web |last1=O'Dea |first1=Colleen |title=2026 Primary: 7th Congressional District |url=https://www.njspotlightnews.org/special-report/2026-primary-7th-congressional-district/ |website=Spotlight New Jersey |access-date=6 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="Daughter"/>

Bennett was deployed to the [[Middle East]] during the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|war in Afghanistan]], serving in a [[carrier strike group]].<ref name="Insider">{{cite web |last1=Rod |first1=Marc |title=From the Strait of Hormuz to the halls of Congress: Rebecca Bennett aims to take on Rep. Tom Kean Jr. |url=https://jewishinsider.com/2025/08/rebecca-bennett-tom-kean-jr-new-jerseys-7th-congressional-district/ |website=Jewish Insider |access-date=8 June 2026 |date=7 August 2025}}</ref> After moving to [[New Jersey]] in 2019,<ref name="Cornell"/> Bennett retired from active duty and joined the reserves.<ref name=":2"/> In 2022, she joined the [[Air National Guard]].<ref name="Hellcat">{{cite web |title=Why 'Hellcats' could be the answer to Democrats troubles |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/06/12/sherrill-spanberger-military-veterans-2026-00401395 |website=POLITICO |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en |date=12 June 2025}}</ref><ref name=":2"/>

===Healthcare===
After relocating to New Jersey, Bennett began working in healthcare.<ref>{{cite web |title=Democratic nominee to take on Tom Kean Jr. has the race to herself — for now |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/03/democrat-rebecca-bennett-tom-kean-jr-midterm-00948885 |website=POLITICO |access-date=6 June 2026 |language=en |date=3 June 2026}}</ref><ref name="Inc"/> She has also worked for [[Noom]], Midi Health, and [[Johnson & Johnson]].<ref name="Monitor">{{cite web |last1=DiFilippo |first1=Dana |title=Four Democrats are vying to challenge Rep. Tom Kean Jr. |url=https://newjerseymonitor.com/2026/05/21/four-democrats-are-vying-to-challenge-rep-thomas-kean-jr/ |website=New Jersey Monitor |access-date=6 June 2026 |date=21 May 2026}}</ref> In 2024, Bennett was listed on ''[[Inc. (magazine)|Inc.]]'' magazine's [[Inc. (magazine)#Initiatives|Best in Business]] program,<ref name="Inc">{{cite web |title=How This Navy Veteran Is Working to Improve Health Care |url=https://www.inc.com/tim-crino/how-this-navy-veteran-is-working-to-improve-healthcare/91064637 |website=Inc. |access-date=6 June 2026}}</ref> and in October that year, she was named vice president for strategic partnerships and network operations at Oshi Health.<ref name=":2"/>

=== Political career ===
{{Also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 7}}
In February 2025, Bennett announced she would seek the Democratic nomination for [[New Jersey's 7th congressional district]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey#District 7|2026 election]].<ref name=":2"/> She won the June 2, 2026, primary election.<ref name="Kean1">{{cite web |title=Rebecca Bennett wins Democratic primary in New Jersey to take on Rep. Tom Kean Jr. |url=https://whyy.org/articles/new-jersey-election-2026-primary-kean-7th-district/ |website=WHYY |access-date=8 June 2026}}</ref> Alongside [[JoAnna Mendoza]], [[Cait Conley]], and [[Maura Sullivan]], she is a member of the Hell Cats, a group of Democratic female veterans who ran in competitive districts in 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Four Female Veterans Running for Congress Launch: "The Hell Cats" - Insider NJ |url=https://www.insidernj.com/press-release/four-female-veterans-running-for-congress-launch-the-hell-cats/ |website=Insider NJ |access-date=8 June 2026}}</ref>

Bennett named New Jersey governor [[Mikie Sherrill]], who is also former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot, as her motivation to run for public office.<ref name=":2"/> She has described herself as a [[moderate Democrat]].<ref name="Daughter" /><ref name="NJ" /> She won the November 3, 2026, general election.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Haberman |first1=Maggie |last2=Epstein |first2=Reid J. |last3=Cohn ==Personal life==
Bennett lives in [[Bridgewater Township, New Jersey]] with her husband, Alex,<ref name="Ballot"/> and their two daughters.<ref name="Daughter">{{cite web |last1=Fox |first1=Joey |title=Rebecca Bennett, ex-Navy helicopter pilot, will run against Kean in NJ-7 |url=https://newjerseyglobe.com/congress/rebecca-bennett-ex-navy-helicopter-pilot-will-run-against-kean-in-nj-7/ |website=New Jersey Globe |access-date=6 June 2026 |date=4 February 2025}}</ref><ref name="NJ">{{cite web |title=Navy helicopter pilot and mom (no, not Gov. Sherrill) wins Dem nomination to take on Tom Kean Jr. |url=https://www.nj.com/news/2026/06/navy-helicopter-pilot-and-mom-no-not-gov-sherrill-wins-dem-nomination-to-take-on-tom-kean-jr.html |website=NJ |access-date=6 June 2026}}</ref>
